scenario: A startup ecosystem report covers only companies that achieved an exit (acquisition or IPO) valued above $10M. A policy maker uses the report's average exit value to set return expectations for a public innovation fund.

data.description: Report only covers exits > $10M. Underlying distribution of all exit values (including failed startups with $0 exit) assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $15M.

values.note: Failed startups exit at approximately $0; $0 is below threshold

question: Covered exits average $30M. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean exit value Î¼ across ALL startups funded (including failures), and (b) the fraction of funded startups that achieve a qualifying exit.
naive_answer: The typical startup exit is worth approximately $30M since that is the report average.
naive_trap: The report excludes all exits under $10M and all total failures. The true mean across the full cohort is about $26M â€” $4M lower â€” and 14% of startups never achieve even a $10M exit. A policy maker expecting $30M average returns would overprice the fund's portfolio.

from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(10-mu)/15; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+15*norm.pdf(a)/sf-30 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,20,29)
assert abs(mu-26.07)<0.5
assert abs(norm.sf((10-mu)/15)-0.8580)<0.01
